security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only Markdown, and most static alerts are false positives from comments, Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and project-local .venv paths. The install examples still include remote script execution and a ~/.bashrc write, which are real risks if an agent or user runs them without confirmation.

remediation.issue: Remote installer scripts are piped directly into a shell or PowerShell.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer package managers such as pip, Homebrew, or a pinned release, and add explicit checksum or signature verification before execution.
Tell users to review and edit shell startup files manually, or use a temporary PATH update for the current session.

remediation.issue: The cargo install example pulls from a Git URL without pinning a commit.
remediation.suggestion: Use a published package or pin source installs to a trusted tag or commit when documenting reproducible setup.

content.value_statement: Python dependency tools can be slow and inconsistent across local, CI, and container workflows. This skill gives uv commands and patterns for faster installs, virtual environments, lockfiles, and migration.
actual_capabilities: Explains uv installation, project initialization, and version checks across macOS, Linux, Windows, pip, Homebrew, and cargo.
Shows dependency operations for adding, removing, upgrading, locking, syncing, and exporting packages.
Covers virtual environment creation, activation, uv run workflows, and Python version pinning.
Provides examples for pyproject.toml, workspaces, Docker builds, GitHub Actions, pre-commit, and VS Code.
Includes troubleshooting steps for PATH issues, Python version mismatches, dependency conflicts, cache problems, and stale lockfiles.
limitations: It gives guidance only; it cannot verify package trust or execute uv commands by itself.
Some install examples rely on external networks and should be reviewed before use.
It does not replace official uv documentation for new or changed features.
It assumes a Python project context and does not cover non-Python package managers.

use_cases.title: Start a Fast Python Project
use_cases.description: Initialize a uv project, pin Python, add runtime and development dependencies, and run tests through uv.

use_cases.title: Speed Up CI Builds
use_cases.description: Use lockfiles, frozen installs, cache reuse, and GitHub Actions patterns to make Python CI more reproducible.

use_cases.title: Migrate Existing Projects
use_cases.description: Move from pip, requirements files, pip-tools, or Poetry while preserving existing project metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to plan a new Python web API project. Include setup steps, dependency groups, and verification commands.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate From pip
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to migrate an existing requirements.txt project to uv. Keep the workflow simple and explain each file change.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CI With Lockfiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv skill to design a GitHub Actions workflow with frozen installs, caching, tests, and dependency updates.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Monorepo Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv skill to propose a workspace layout for three Python packages with shared tooling, lockfile policy, and Docker guidance.

output_examples.input: I need to migrate a small Flask service from pip to uv.
output_examples.output: A migration plan with inventory steps, uv initialization guidance, dependency syncing, lockfile handling, test verification, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: Our CI installs Python dependencies too slowly.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for uv caching, frozen syncs, lockfile use, parallel installs, and a clear verification checklist.

output_examples.input: I need Docker guidance for a uv project.
output_examples.output: A Docker workflow outline that separates dependency installation from application code and explains how to keep builds reproducible.

best_practices: Commit uv.lock for applications and use frozen installs in CI.
Review install commands before executing remote scripts or modifying shell startup files.
Prefer uv run for project commands so environments stay consistent.
anti_patterns: Piping installer scripts to a shell without confirmation or integrity checks.
Editing global shell startup files when a project-local PATH change is enough.
Mixing pip, Poetry, and uv commands without a clear migration plan.

faq.question: What is uv?
faq.answer: uv is a fast Python package and project manager that handles dependencies, virtual environments, Python versions, and lockfiles.

faq.question: Can this skill help migrate from pip or Poetry?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes migration patterns from requirements files, pip-tools, and Poetry to uv workflows.

faq.question: Does it support CI and Docker workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides patterns for GitHub Actions, lockfile installs, caching, and Docker build optimization.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent must decide which commands are appropriate.

faq.question: Are remote installer commands safe?
faq.answer: They can be risky because they execute downloaded code. Review the source, prefer package managers, and seek confirmation first.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot uv errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common PATH, Python version, dependency resolution, cache, and lockfile issues.
